title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 19
paragraphs: In the twelfth year of the war, while the standing corn was being burned by the Lydian army, this happened. As soon as the corn was set ablaze, the fire was carried by a strong wind and set fire to the temple of Athena called Athena of Assesos, and the temple burned to the ground. At the time no account was taken of it, but afterwards, when the army had returned to Sardis, Alyattes fell sick, and as the sickness went on long, he sent messengers to consult the oracle at Delphi — either advised by someone to do so, or because he himself thought it best to send and ask the god about his illness. But when the messengers arrived at Delphi, the Pythian prophetess refused to give them any answer until they had rebuilt the temple of Athena which they had burned at Assesos in Milesian territory.
